diagnostics.message: module.aws_iam_elastic_stack:output.access_key_id: explicit depends_on of module.aws_iam_elastic_stack:resource.aws_iam_access_key.this_user is redundant — already implied by attribute references
module.aws_iam_elastic_stack:output.access_secret_key: explicit depends_on of module.aws_iam_elastic_stack:resource.aws_iam_access_key.this_user is redundant — already implied by attribute references

helm_release.elk deploys Elasticsearch configured with secretKeyRefs to secret "elastic-credentials" (extraEnvs ELASTIC_PASSWORD/ELASTIC_USERNAME), but has no dependency on kubernetes_secret.elasticsearch_credentials, so pods can be scheduled before the secret exists.

helm_release.elk mounts secret "elastic-certificates" into Elasticsearch, Kibana, Filebeat and APM pods (secretMounts / TLS config), but has no dependency on kubernetes_secret.elasticsearch_certificates.

helm_release.elk configures the Elasticsearch keystore from secret "elasticsearch-s3-user-creds" (S3 snapshot repository credentials), but has no dependency on kubernetes_secret.elasticsearch_s3_user_creds.
helm_release.elk deploys Kibana which reads KIBANA_ENCRYPTION_KEY from secret "kibana-encryption-key", but the release has no dependency on kubernetes_secret.kibana_enc_key.
Output access_secret_key already references aws_iam_access_key.this_user in its value, so the explicit depends_on duplicates an implicit dependency.
Output access_key_id already references aws_iam_access_key.this_user in its value, so the explicit depends_on duplicates an implicit dependency.
